questions.stem: The temperatures over a week were: −3°C, 2°C, 5°C, −1°C, 4°C, 0°C, 7°C. What is the range?
questions.explanation: Range = highest − lowest = 7 − (−3) = 7 + 3 = 10°C. A very common error is calculating 7 − 0 = 7 or 7 − 3 = 4, forgetting that the lowest value is negative.

questions.stem: Two data sets have the same mean of 50. Set A has range 10, Set B has range 40. What can you conclude?

options.text: Set A has more data values
Set B is more spread out (less consistent)
Set A has a higher median
Set B has a higher mode

questions.explanation: A larger range indicates more spread or variation in the data. Set B (range 40) is more spread out, meaning the data is less consistent than Set A (range 10). The range tells us nothing about the median or mode.

questions.stem: A data set of 8 values has a range of 15. The smallest value is 4. If the largest value is removed, the new range is 11. What was the second largest value?
questions.explanation: Original largest = smallest + range = 4 + 15 = 19. After removing 19, new range = 11, so new largest = 4 + 11 = 15. The second largest value is 15.

questions.stem: The values 3, 5, 8, 12, x have a range of 14. What are the possible values of x?
questions.explanation: If x is the largest: x − 3 = 14, so x = 17. If x is the smallest: 12 − x = 14, so x = −2. Both give range 14. If 3 ≤ x ≤ 12, the range is 12 − 3 = 9, not 14. So x = 17 or x = −2.

questions.stem: Five values have a mean of 20 and a range of 12. The smallest value is 14. What is the sum of the other four values?
questions.explanation: Total sum = 5 x 20 = 100. The sum of the other four values = 100 − 14 = 86. (We know the largest = 14 + 12 = 26, which is one of the four, but the question just asks for the sum of the other four.)
